pages.name: Share the strip
pages.text: `x² + 6x` is an `x` by `x` square with a strip 6 wide beside it. Cut the strip in half and swing one half round to the bottom, so both sides grow by 3. The pieces nearly make a square with sides `x + 3`, missing a 3 by 3 corner, so `x² + 6x` is `(x + 3)² − 9`.

pages.name: The corner for 8
pages.task: Cut the strip of `x² + 8x` in half and swing one half round. What is the missing corner?
pages.why: Half of 8 is 4, so each side grows by 4 and the corner is 4 by 4, which is 16. So `x² + 8x` is `(x + 4)² − 16`, and at `x = 1` both give 9.

pages.name: Any b
pages.text: Whatever `b` is, half of it goes on each side, so the corner is `(b ÷ 2)²`. Add the corner and take it off again, and nothing changes, so `x² + bx` is `(x + b ÷ 2)²` less the corner. This move is called [[completing the square]].

pages.name: Which form?
pages.task: Which is `x² + 10x` with its square completed?
pages.why: Half of 10 is 5, so the square is `(x + 5)²`, and its 5 by 5 corner, 25, comes off again. At `x = 1`, `1 + 10 = 11` and `36 − 25 = 11`.

pages.task: Lesson 2 found no whole-number pair for `x² + 4x + 1`. Which is it with its square completed?
pages.why: Half of 4 is 2, so the corner is 2 by 2, which is 4. The 1 fills one of its squares and leaves 3 empty, so it is `(x + 2)² − 4 + 1`, which is `(x + 2)² − 3`. At `x = 1` both give 6.

pages.name: The turning point
pages.text: `(x + 3)²` is never below zero, and it is zero at `x = −3`, so `(x + 3)² − 7` is lowest there, at −7. That bottom of the U, `(−3, −7)`, is its [[turning point]], and since points the same distance either side of −3 give the same square, the curve is a mirror image about the line `x = −3`, its [[line of symmetry]]. Slide `b` and the turning point moves to `x = −b ÷ 2`, dropping by the corner.

pages.name: Read the turning point
pages.task: Where is the turning point of `(x − 4)² + 3`?
pages.why: The square is zero when `x − 4 = 0`, at `x = 4`, and there the value is the 3 outside. So the turning point is `(4, 3)`. The graph is `y = x²` slid 4 right and 3 up.

pages.name: Solve it
pages.text: To solve `x² + 6x + 2 = 0`, take the 2 across and add the corner, 9, to both sides, so `(x + 3)² = 7`. Then `x + 3` is `√7` or `−√7`, about 2.65 or −2.65. So `x` is about −0.35 or −5.65, where the curve crosses the axis.

pages.name: The next line
pages.task: Solving `x² + 4x + 1 = 0`, the first line is `x² + 4x = −1`. What is the next line?
pages.why: Add the corner, 4, to both sides, so the left becomes `(x + 2)²` and the right `−1 + 4 = 3`. Then `x + 2` is `√3` or `−√3`, and `x` is about −0.27 or −3.73.

pages.name: Upside down
pages.text: With a minus in front of `x²`, take it out first, so `−x² + 4x + 10` is `−(x² − 4x) + 10`. Inside, half of −4 is −2, so the bracket is `x − 2`, and the minus in front turns its −4 into +4: `−(x − 2)² + 14`. The square is never below zero, so this is never above 14, its highest point, at `x = 2`.

pages.name: Mixed: a 2 in front
pages.task: Which is `2x² + 12x + 5` with its square completed?
pages.why: Take the 2 out of the first two terms, so `2(x² + 6x) + 5`. Then `x² + 6x` is `(x + 3)² − 9`, and the 9 comes off twice, `2 × 9 = 18`. So it is `2(x + 3)² − 13`, and at `x = 1` both give 19.

pages.task: Where is the lowest point of `x² − 10x + 30`?
pages.why: Half of −10 is −5, so it is `(x − 5)² − 25 + 30`, which is `(x − 5)² + 5`. The square is zero at `x = 5`, so the lowest point is `(5, 5)`.

pages.name: Mixed: a minus in front
pages.task: Which is `−x² + 6x − 4` with its square completed?
pages.why: Take the minus out first, so `−(x² − 6x) − 4`. Half of −6 is −3, so `x² − 6x` is `(x − 3)² − 9`, and the minus in front turns −9 into +9: `−(x − 3)² + 9 − 4`, which is `−(x − 3)² + 5`. Its highest point is `(3, 5)`, and at `x = 1` both give 1.
